title: The Minotaur and the Ministry: Palaio Faliro, Essex, Sydney, and the Five Months on Nikis Street
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Palaio Faliro, and the House That Argued

stops.name: Palaio Faliro, the house on Parthenonos Street
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the municipality (Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis'); the street address and the character of the household come from family memoir and profile writing, and the coordinate is an approximation of central Palaio Faliro rather than a verified door
stops.campa: A son is born in Palaio Faliro, on the flat coastal edge of Athens where the city runs out into the Saronic Gulf. His father Georgios has been imprisoned for his politics; his mother is an activist in her own right. The house on Parthenonos Street is one where argument is the ordinary weather of the dinner table, and certain conversations there are conducted in a code the children are expected to learn young. The registry for the municipality writes the child down as Ioannis Georgiou Varoufakis, born the twenty-fourth of March 1961.
suggested_refs: Raise Your Soul: A Personal History of Resistance (2025), his own reconstruction of the household through five women of his family
sources: thetoc.gr obituary of Georgios Varoufakis (d. 28 September 2021), reproducing the family account

stops.name: Palaio Faliro, the morning of the colonels
stops.date_confidence: the coup itself is attested to 21 April 1967; everything domestic here is family recollection reported at second hand and is reconstruction, not record
stops.campa: Before dawn the tanks take the streets of Athens and a group of colonels takes the state. In the family's account relatives are arrested, and the coded speech of the household stops being a habit and becomes a precaution: names are not said, opinions are folded inside other opinions, and a child learns which sentences may be spoken outdoors and which may not. He is six years old on the morning it starts. The colonels hold Greece for seven years, and he is seventeen when they go.
suggested_refs: The Greek military junta of 1967-1974 and the political imprisonments of its first months
sources: thetoc.gr obituary of Georgios Varoufakis, family account cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Psychiko, the Moraitis School and the single n
stops.date_confidence: attendance is attested (the Moraitis School's own alumni list names him); the spelling anecdote is self-reported and undated, and the year here is an ordering device covering the school years, not a record of anything that happened in 1972
stops.campa: He is sent to the Moraitis School in Psychiko, on the far side of Athens from the sea, a private school for the children of the professional classes. There, by his own telling, he begins spelling his name with a single n, Yanis rather than Yannis. It is a small stubbornness about the shape of a name, practised long before he has any public use for one, and the school's alumni lists carry him under it now. A teacher marks it wrong. He keeps the spelling.
suggested_refs: The Moraitis School alumni register, Psychiko, which lists him among its graduates
sources: profile interviews cited in the research dossier (self-reported anecdote)

segments.name: Essex, and the Optimization of Strikes

stops.name: Wivenhoe Park, arrival at seventeen
stops.date_confidence: the departure for Britain at seventeen and the Essex enrolment are attested; the month is conventional for a British academic year and is not itself recorded
stops.campa: He arrives in England months after the colonels have gone and Greek democracy has been restored, sent by parents who want their son out of a country that has just demonstrated what it can do to one. He enrols at Essex intending to read physics and turns to economics instead. The campus at Wivenhoe Park is concrete set down in Colchester parkland, and it is politically loud. He joins the Communist Society and the Troops Out Movement and serves as secretary of the Black Students Alliance, arguing that black is a political identity and not only an ethnic one.
suggested_refs: Simon Usborne's Independent profile of 3 February 2015, source of the Black Students Alliance account

stops.name: Edgbaston, the mathematics of bargaining
stops.date_confidence: attested that he moved to Birmingham in 1981 for an MSc in mathematical statistics, completed 1982; the month is conventional
stops.campa: He moves inland to Birmingham for a master's degree in mathematical statistics, a single year at Edgbaston. It is the technical training that will let him spend the next decade doing mathematical economics with a straight face while disbelieving a good deal of what the discipline claims for itself. The mathematics he is learning is the mathematics of bargaining: what two parties do when neither can compel the other and the threat of inflicting cost is the only currency either side holds. He submits the degree in 1982.
suggested_refs: The University of Birmingham MSc in Mathematical Statistics, 1981-1982

stops.name: Norwich, the price of tea and coffee
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Wikipedia confirms a post at East Anglia between Essex and Cambridge but gives no years at all, and the 1985-1988 window rests solely on his 2013 curriculum vitae, which was not re-fetched for this file
stops.campa: He holds a research post and a lectureship at East Anglia, on the low flat campus outside Norwich, and does the ordinary work of a young econometrician: forecasting the price of tea and coffee, modelling wage inflation. It is unglamorous, and it is teaching him exactly how the discipline earns its keep, which commodity series it trusts and which it quietly drops. The published record does not fix the years he is there. The only account of them is his own curriculum vitae.
suggested_refs: Varoufakis's early econometric papers on commodity price forecasting and wage inflation
sources: Varoufakis academic CV (yanisvaroufakis.eu, 2013), cited in the research dossier
Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis' (names the post, supplies no dates)

stops.name: Colchester, On Optimization and Strikes
stops.date_confidence: the 1987 award, the thesis title and Monojit Chatterji as supervisor are attested; the named examiners appear only in the 2013 curriculum vitae and are reconstruction; no month is recorded
stops.campa: He takes his doctorate at Essex for a thesis titled On Optimization and Strikes, supervised by Monojit Chatterji: game theory turned on industrial conflict, the strike written out as a bargaining problem with the arithmetic exposed. Twenty-eight years later he will sit inside that structure at a table in Brussels, with a country in the place of a factory. A strike, on this account, is what happens when two sides who need each other conclude that hurting each other is the cheaper road to agreement, and that the pain has to be visible to work.
suggested_refs: On Optimization and Strikes, University of Essex doctoral thesis, 1987, also catalogued as Optimisation and Strikes

stops.name: Camperdown, a lectureship at the other end of the world
stops.date_confidence: attested that he moved to Sydney and joined the university in 1988; no month recorded
stops.campa: He crosses to the other side of the planet and takes a lectureship at the University of Sydney, in the sandstone quadrangle at Camperdown. Greece from here is a country reached by telephone and by newspapers that arrive late. He will stay more than a decade, rising to senior lecturer, publishing on bargaining and game theory, arguing in public against John Howard's government, and building the Greek-Australian networks that keep an Athens politics alive at twelve thousand miles.
suggested_refs: The University of Sydney economics department in the Howard years, and the Greek-Australian political networks of the period

stops.name: Oxford Street, Sydney, one tablet
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from his own recollection thirty-seven years later: he places it at a Sydney Mardi Gras, which falls in late February or early March, and the year 1989 comes from the dossier's reading of the podcast account, not from any contemporaneous record
stops.campa: At a Mardi Gras in Sydney he takes one tablet of ecstasy. He dances, by his own count, fifteen or sixteen hours. A migraine follows that lasts a week and he never repeats the experiment. He is twenty-eight, an economics lecturer with a doctorate on strikes, and the episode is a single night in a life otherwise conducted at desks and in seminar rooms. He tells nobody in particular and does not think about it again for decades. Thirty-seven years later a prosecutor in Athens reads a transcript of him describing it.
suggested_refs: His account on Gaia Mercouri's podcast 3026: Human Algorithm, January 2026
sources: Reuters, 'Greece's ex-finance minister Varoufakis charged over use of dance drug ecstasy', 26 February 2026

stops.name: Camperdown, the passport and Rational Conflict
stops.date_confidence: the naturalisation and the Blackwell publication are both placed in 1991 by attested sources; no months recorded
stops.campa: Australia issues him a passport, and he becomes and remains a dual national, Greek and Australian both. The same year Blackwell publishes Rational Conflict, the monograph on bargaining and strikes that is the doctorate grown into a book. It goes to university libraries and to the small scattered readership that works on bargaining models. He is a working academic economist in the ordinary sense: a research programme, a teaching load, a second country whose politics he argues about in its letters pages.
suggested_refs: Rational Conflict (Oxford: Blackwell, 1991)

stops.name: Gilmorehill, teaching a discipline and dismantling it
stops.date_confidence: the Glasgow appointment is attested but undated in every source reachable for this file; the 1995-1996 window is reconstruction from the curriculum vitae, and it is placed here to sit beside the book, which is firmly dated to 1995
stops.campa: He takes a senior lectureship at Glasgow, on Gilmorehill under the Gothic spire, one of the short northern appointments that punctuate the Sydney years; a Hoover fellowship takes him to Louvain in the same stretch. In 1995 Routledge publishes Game Theory: A Critical Introduction, written with Shaun Hargreaves Heap. The textbook teaches the whole apparatus and then takes it apart, arguing that game theory cannot deliver the determinate account of rational action it advertises. No source reachable now gives the years of the Glasgow post.
suggested_refs: Game Theory: A Critical Introduction, with Shaun Hargreaves Heap (London: Routledge, 1995)
sources: Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis' (short appointments at Glasgow and Louvain, no years given)

stops.name: Panepistimiou Street, the chair of economic theory
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 2000 appointment as associate professor and the 2005 full professorship; no months recorded
stops.campa: He comes home. The National and Kapodistrian University of Athens appoints him associate professor, and in 2005 professor of economic theory, in the painted neoclassical building on Panepistimiou. Greece in these years is inside the euro and borrowing at something close to German interest rates, which everyone treats as a fact about Greece rather than a fact about the euro. He founds UADPhilEcon, the doctoral programme in economics, and spends the decade producing students, textbooks and a widening public voice.
suggested_refs: UADPhilEcon, the University of Athens doctoral programme in economics that he founded

stops.name: Charilaou Trikoupi, advising Papandreou
stops.date_confidence: the advisory role to George Papandreou from 2004 is attested; the venue is reconstruction, placed at the PASOK headquarters on Charilaou Trikoupi because no specific meeting place is recorded anywhere reachable
stops.campa: He advises George Papandreou, leader of PASOK, on economic policy. It is an insider's apprenticeship in how Greek parties actually decide things, and he will spend years afterwards disowning it: when Papandreou's government signs the first bailout memorandum in 2010, Varoufakis becomes one of its loudest and most technical opponents. What survives of the advisory work is the relationship, and then the repudiation of the relationship. No minutes of it are public, and no reachable source names a room the two men met in.
suggested_refs: PASOK headquarters, Charilaou Trikoupi 50, Athens

stops.name: Ledra Street, the line through the capital
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: that he travelled with Danae Stratou while she documented seven barriers for Cut is reported, and Cyprus is on the documented list, but no reachable source pins the crossing point they used or the month
stops.campa: With Danae Stratou he travels some sixty thousand kilometres so that she can photograph seven divided landscapes for the work she calls Cut: Seven Dividing Lines. Nicosia is one of them, a capital sawn in half by a buffer zone the United Nations patrols. He is the companion on this journey and not the artist, and he is also an economist standing at a border, watching what a line does to a small economy that has one running through its middle. At Ledra Street the barrier narrows to a crossing point, and the two halves of the city can look at each other across it.
suggested_refs: Danae Stratou, Cut: Seven Dividing Lines (2007), and its documentation of the Nicosia Green Line
sources: research dossier account of the Cut project's barrier list; exact site not independently confirmed

stops.name: Friendship Park, the fence into the Pacific
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on the same footing as Nicosia: the United States-Mexico border is on the documented Cut list, the specific crossing point is inferred, and the month is an ordering device with no source behind it
stops.campa: The same journey reaches the Pacific end of the United States-Mexico border, where the barrier runs down the sand and on into the surf at Friendship Park. Of the seven barriers the project documents, this is the one built by the richest country in the survey, and it is made of the same corrugated steel as the rest. Stratou photographs the line. He walks it. Families stand on opposite sides of the mesh and talk through it, an arrangement the guards permit at certain hours.
suggested_refs: Friendship Park, inside Border Field State Park, San Diego-Tijuana
sources: research dossier account of the Cut project; Wikipedia, 'Friendship Park (San Diego-Tijuana)' for the site

stops.name: Athens, the Modest Proposal and the Minotaur
stops.date_confidence: the Modest Proposal is dated to 2010 and The Global Minotaur to 2011; neither carries a recorded day, and the stop is pinned at his university rather than at any publisher's address
stops.campa: With Stuart Holland he issues A Modest Proposal for Resolving the Euro Crisis, arguing that the institutions Europe already possesses could carry the debt without a federal treasury and without a new treaty. The following year Zed Books publishes The Global Minotaur, his account of the arrangement that ran the world after 1971: the United States running deficits on purpose, drawing in the planet's surpluses and pumping them back out, a beast in a labyrinth fed on tribute until the machinery that fed it broke in 2008.
suggested_refs: A Modest Proposal for Resolving the Euro Crisis, with Stuart Holland and later James K. Galbraith
The Global Minotaur (London: Zed Books, 2011)

stops.name: Bellevue, economist to a country that does not exist
stops.date_confidence: the Valve appointment in 2012 is attested; no month recorded, and the Bellevue coordinate is an approximation of the company's headquarters rather than a verified address
stops.campa: Gabe Newell reads his writing on the euro and hires him as economist-in-residence at Valve, in Bellevue across the water from Seattle. He is set to study economies that exist only inside games: the hat trade of Team Fortress 2, the item markets of Dota 2, the exchange rates between them, every transaction logged. It is a dataset no national statistician has ever had, a complete economy with no dark corners. He calls the company's flat, bossless structure an enlightened oligarchy.
suggested_refs: The Valve Economics blog, 2012-2013, where his in-game economy analyses were published
sources: gamedeveloper.com and Valve Economics posts cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Austin, the LBJ School and Galbraith
stops.date_confidence: the visiting professorship at the LBJ School is attested but carries no years in any reachable source; 2013 is the dossier's placement and the years are reconstruction
stops.campa: At the LBJ School in Austin he holds a visiting professorship and works beside James K. Galbraith, co-author with him and Stuart Holland of the later versions of the Modest Proposal. Texas is where the European argument gets rehearsed in front of Americans with no stake in it, which is a useful test of whether it survives outside its own weather. Galbraith will be in Athens two years later, inside the Greek contingency planning of 2015. How many semesters Varoufakis spends in Austin is not recorded anywhere.
suggested_refs: James K. Galbraith's own account of the 2015 Greek contingency planning
sources: Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis' (lists the UT Austin visiting post, no years)
research dossier synthesis of the 2012-2013 Texas period

stops.name: Zagreb, the lecture that becomes a finger
stops.date_confidence: the Subversive Festival is held every May in Zagreb with keynote lectures at Kino Europa and lists him among its 2013 guests; the day is not recorded, and the dossier's original attribution of the lecture to the Faculty of Economics and Business is an error corrected here
stops.campa: At the Subversive Festival in Zagreb, in the old Kino Europa on Varsavska, he tells an audience what Greece ought to have done in 2010: default inside the euro, and tell Germany where to put the loan. He is a professor with no office to lose. Two years later a fragment of the video, stripped of its conditional tense and its date, will run across Germany as proof that the sitting Greek finance minister has raised his middle finger at the country. A satirist then confesses to faking the clip, and the confession is itself the hoax.
suggested_refs: Jan Bohmermann's Neo Magazin Royale segment of March 2015 claiming to have forged the video
sources: The Atlantic, 'Giving Germany the Middle Finger', March 2015 (cited in the dossier; the domain refused direct fetch)

stops.name: Syntagma Square, elected for Athens B
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: He stands for Syriza in Athens B, having briefed Alexis Tsipras since 2013 on what a Syriza government could actually do inside the euro, and takes one of the largest personal preference votes any first-time candidate has drawn. He is fifty-three, an academic with an Australian passport, newly a member of the Greek parliament for a party that has never governed anything. Syriza wins the election. In the square below Parliament that evening a crowd celebrates the end of the memoranda as an accomplished fact.
suggested_refs: Hellenic Parliament records for the Athens B constituency, January 2015
sources: hellenicparliament.gr, cited in the research dossier

stops.name: Nikis 5, the finance ministry
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the ministry's address on Nikis at Syntagma is confirmed against the ministry's own record, correcting a Syngrou Avenue coordinate carried in the research dossier
stops.campa: Two days after the election Tsipras makes him finance minister in the coalition with the Independent Greeks. The ministry stands at Nikis 5, on Syntagma, its windows over the square where the anti-austerity crowds massed for five years. His stated brief is neither default nor exit: restructure the debt down to what can actually be paid, and stop the austerity that keeps shrinking the economy the debt is measured against. Greece has been in depression for six years and has lost roughly a quarter of its output.
stops.quote: Europe in its infinite wisdom decided to deal with this bankruptcy by loading the largest loan in human history on the weakest of shoulders.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to a BBC News interview, 3 February 2015; seen only on Wikiquote, the broadcast original being unreachable for this file
suggested_refs: Ministry of National Economy and Finance, Nikis 5-7, Syntagma Square, Athens
sources: Wikipedia, 'Ministry of National Economy and Finance (Greece)'

stops.name: Nikis 5, the press conference with Dijsselbloem
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the encounter is reported everywhere in contemporaneous journalism but every outlet holding the primary account refused fetching for this file, so it rests on the research dossier alone
stops.campa: Jeroen Dijsselbloem, president of the Eurogroup, comes to Athens three days into the new government. At the press conference Varoufakis says Greece will negotiate with the legitimate institutions of Europe but will not accept the troika, a body he describes as self-appointed and without foundation in any treaty, as its interlocutor. Dijsselbloem leans in, says something the microphones do not catch, and leaves. The photographs of the handshake are around the world within the hour.
suggested_refs: Contemporaneous video of the Varoufakis-Dijsselbloem press conference, Athens, 30 January 2015
sources: research dossier account; no primary source re-fetched

stops.name: Frankfurt, the waiver lifted
stops.date_confidence: the Governing Council decision is attested to the day at the ECB's own press archive; the meeting with Mario Draghi in the same week rests on the dossier alone and is reconstruction
stops.campa: He goes to Frankfurt to see Mario Draghi, whose institution holds the tap that keeps Greek banks open. On the same day the Governing Council lifts the waiver that had allowed Greek government paper to be pledged as collateral in Eurosystem operations, on the ground that it can no longer assume the bailout review will be completed. From this day the negotiation runs on a clock the Greek side does not hold. The banks are pushed onto emergency liquidity assistance, which is dearer, and which the Governing Council renews or declines to renew every fortnight.
stops.quote: The Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB) today decided to lift the waiver affecting marketable debt instruments issued or fully guaranteed by the Hellenic Republic.
stops.quote_source: European Central Bank press release, Frankfurt, 4 February 2015 (this is the ECB speaking, not Varoufakis)
suggested_refs: ECB press release pr150204, 4 February 2015, on the Greek collateral waiver

stops.name: Berlin, agreeing to disagree
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Berlin leg of the February capitals tour and the Schauble meeting come from the research dossier and were not independently re-fetched; the day is the dossier's ordering, not a recorded date
stops.campa: In Berlin he meets Wolfgang Schauble, finance minister of Germany, the man who will determine more than any other what the negotiation is permitted to contain. Varoufakis will later describe the whole affair as a war of attrition between two very different opponents. Nothing at this meeting is agreed and nothing is signed, and the phrase that survives it is the closest the two men come to a joint position in five months. Asked at the joint press conference whether they found common ground, Schauble says they agreed to disagree.
stops.quote: an attrition war between a reasonably numerate villain (the IMF) and a chronic procrastinator (Berlin)
stops.quote_source: Varoufakis, 4 April 2015, on the tensions between the IMF and Germany over Greek debt, as quoted on Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis'
suggested_refs: The Varoufakis-Schauble joint press conference, Bundesministerium der Finanzen, Berlin, February 2015

stops.name: Brussels, the four-month extension
stops.date_confidence: the Eurogroup statement of 20 February 2015 is attested, though the Council's own PDF refused fetching for this file; the coordinate is the atlas's canonical Brussels pin rather than the Justus Lipsius building itself, which stands about three kilometres east
stops.campa: In the Justus Lipsius building the Eurogroup and Greece agree to extend the Master Financial Assistance Facility by four months. Two earlier meetings, on the eleventh and the sixteenth, had broken up with no agreed language at all. Varoufakis presents the extension as room bought for a comprehensive settlement. On the Greek left it is read at once as the first capitulation, the moment a government elected to break the frame accepted the frame. The agreed text is short, and it says very little. Both readings are defensible from it.
suggested_refs: Eurogroup statement on Greece, 20 February 2015, extending the Master Financial Assistance Facility Agreement
sources: consilium.europa.eu Eurogroup statement of 20 February 2015 (cited in the dossier; fetch refused)

stops.name: Plaka, the photographs on the terrace
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Paris Match feature and his subsequent regret are reported in March 2015, and the fifteenth is the filing date of the Guardian piece the dossier cites rather than the date of the shoot
stops.campa: Paris Match photographs the finance minister and Danae Stratou at home in Plaka, the Acropolis lit behind them and a table laid. The pictures run while Greek pensioners are queueing at cash machines. The phrase that attaches itself is white-wine socialism, and it sticks harder than anything he has said about debt sustainability. Those photographs and the motorcycle remain the most reproduced images of him out of the whole of 2015. He says afterwards that he regrets the shoot.
suggested_refs: The Paris Match feature of March 2015 and the Guardian interview in which he says he regrets it
sources: theguardian.com, 15 March 2015, cited in the research dossier (domain refused direct fetch)

stops.name: Riga, the words nobody signs
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the informal Eurogroup of 24 April 2015 in Riga is attested, but the insults are anonymous-source journalism that could not be re-fetched for this file, and the coordinate is a central-Riga approximation
stops.campa: At the Eurogroup in Riga the briefing against him turns explicit. The meeting is an informal one and takes no formal decision. Officials speaking to reporters on condition that they not be named call him an amateur, a gambler, a time-waster. The Eurogroup keeps no minutes, and what survives from Riga is a set of quotations attributed to nobody at all. He denies that anyone insulted him in the room, and says he missed the official dinner for an engagement made earlier.
suggested_refs: Guardian live blog of the Riga Eurogroup, 24 April 2015
sources: research dossier synthesis of contemporaneous press accounts; not independently re-fetched

stops.name: Athens, the file taken away
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the reshuffle of the negotiating team around Euclid Tsakalotos on 27 April is reported contemporaneously but was not independently re-fetched for this file
stops.campa: Three days after Riga, Tsipras reorganises the negotiating team and puts Euclid Tsakalotos at its head. Varoufakis keeps the title, the office on Nikis and the seat at the Eurogroup table, and loses the file. He goes on attending the meetings for another ten weeks, a minister whose signature is still required and whose judgement is no longer wanted. The Greek press reads the move within hours as the first stage of his removal; the government denies that reading.
suggested_refs: Reuters reporting of the Greek negotiating-team reshuffle, 27 April 2015
sources: research dossier chronology; Reuters citation not independently re-fetched

stops.name: Brussels, the meeting without Greece
stops.date_confidence: the referendum announcement is attested to 27 June 2015 and the vote to 5 July; the sequence of the 25-27 June Eurogroup sessions is the dossier's, and the coordinate is the canonical Brussels pin
stops.campa: The institutions put a package on the table on the twenty-fifth and the twenty-sixth. In the small hours of the twenty-seventh, from Athens, Tsipras goes on television and calls a referendum on it. The Eurogroup reconvenes in the Justus Lipsius building the same day and continues without the Greek finance minister in the room, an arrangement Varoufakis argues has no basis in any treaty. Nobody produces the rule that permits it, and the meeting goes ahead.
suggested_refs: The Eurogroup sessions of 25-27 June 2015 and the announcement of the Greek bailout referendum

stops.name: Athens, the night of the No
stops.date_confidence: the referendum result of 61.31 percent against is attested; the bank closure, capital controls and IMF arrears of 29-30 June are reported contemporaneously but were not re-fetched; the inner-cabinet vote is his own memoir account and other participants dispute it
stops.campa: The banks have been shut since the twenty-ninth of June, capital controls in force, withdrawals capped at sixty euro a day, and on the thirtieth Greece missed a payment of roughly one and a half billion to the IMF. On the fifth of July, asked whether to accept the creditors' proposal, 61.31 percent of Greek voters say no. That night, by his own account, Varoufakis puts three measures to the inner cabinet: haircut the bonds the ECB holds, switch on a parallel payments system, take control of the Bank of Greece. He is outvoted four to two.
stops.quote: Why did they force us to close the banks? To instil fear in people.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to The Guardian, 4 July 2015; seen only on Wikiquote, the original being unreachable for this file
suggested_refs: Adults in the Room (2017), his account of the inner-cabinet meeting on the night of the referendum

stops.name: Nikis 5, Minister No More
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, including Tsakalotos being sworn in as his successor the same day
stops.campa: The morning after the referendum he resigns. The creditors, he writes, have made plain that his presence at the Eurogroup is unwelcome and the prime minister has judged that absence helpful, so he goes. The post is headed Minister No More! Euclid Tsakalotos is sworn in later the same day. Within six weeks the government he served accepts a third memorandum harsher than the one 61 percent of the country had just rejected. He leaves office at fifty-four, five months and ten days after entering it.
stops.quote: wear the creditors' loathing with pride
stops.quote_source: Yanis Varoufakis, 'Minister No More!', 6 July 2015, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis'
suggested_refs: 'Minister No More!', yanisvaroufakis.eu, 6 July 2015

stops.name: Geneva, capitalism will eat democracy
stops.date_confidence: TED's own record dates the talk to TEDGlobal>Geneva, December 2015, correcting a London attribution carried in the research dossier; the day is not given and the coordinate is the Geneva conference centre
stops.campa: Five months out of office he gives the talk that carries the argument out of the Greek file and into a general one: capitalism will eat democracy, he says, unless we speak up. The claim is that the economic sphere and the political sphere were separated deliberately, that the decisions which matter most were walled off from anything anybody votes on, and that the wall is what he ran into in Brussels. The audience in the hall has largely never heard of the Master Financial Assistance Facility. TED records the talk, subtitles it and puts it online.
suggested_refs: 'Capitalism will eat democracy, unless we speak up', TEDGlobal>Geneva, December 2015
sources: research dossier list of major talks

stops.name: Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz, the movement launched
stops.date_confidence: the date, the Volksbuhne venue and Srecko Horvat as co-founder are attested; the research dossier's two lenses disagreed on the further names, one giving Julian Assange and the other Ken Loach, and neither appears in the DiEM25 record, so the coordinating collective is given here as the record gives it
stops.campa: He stands on the stage of the Volksbuhne on Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz and launches the Democracy in Europe Movement 2025, founded with the Croatian philosopher Srecko Horvat. The slogan is democratise or disintegrate: either the European Union opens its decision-making to the people it governs by 2025, or it comes apart on its own. Brian Eno, Noam Chomsky, Elif Shafak and Vivienne Westwood sit on the first coordinating collective. A second, ceremonial launch follows in Rome on the twenty-third of March.
stops.quote: those of us who are most critical of Europe have a moral duty to stay in Europe, fight for it, and democratise it
stops.quote_source: Varoufakis at a Guardian Live event on the EU referendum, 24 October 2015, as quoted on Wikipedia, 'Yanis Varoufakis'
suggested_refs: The DiEM25 manifesto and the 2016 coordinating collective

stops.name: Athens, Adults in the Room
stops.date_confidence: the 2017 publication is attested; no month recorded, and the stop is pinned in Athens where the book was written rather than at its London publisher
stops.campa: He publishes Adults in the Room: My Battle with Europe's Deep Establishment, an account of the 2015 negotiation built in part from recordings he made himself. It names people and reproduces what they said in rooms that kept no minutes, and every person named disputes some part of it. The Guardian will later place it eighty-sixth in a list of the hundred best books of the century. Costa-Gavras films it in 2019 with Christos Loulis in the part, staging the European officials as a chorus moving in synchronised unison against a humanised Greek side.

stops.name: Athens, the disobedience front
stops.date_confidence: the party's own record gives 27 March 2018 in Athens; the Guardian filed its launch story on the twenty-sixth, which is where the dossier's competing date comes from; the venue is not identified anywhere reachable and the coordinate is central Athens
stops.campa: He founds MeRA25, the European Realistic Disobedience Front, the Greek wing of the movement launched in Berlin two years earlier. The name is the programme: not exit, not obedience, but refusal to comply with rules the party holds illegitimate while putting alternatives on the table inside the institutions that make them. The constituency he says he wants is people of the left and liberalism, greens and feminists. Whether that coalition exists in Greece is the question the next election will answer.

stops.name: Thessaloniki, back into the chamber
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, including the 3.44 percent share and the nine seats
stops.campa: MeRA25 takes 3.44 percent in the national election, clearing the three percent threshold by less than half a point, and wins nine seats. He is elected for Thessaloniki A, a northern constituency four hundred kilometres from the district that first sent him to Parliament. Four years after resigning he sits again in the chamber on Syntagma, on the opposition benches, with eight colleagues and no ministry. Syriza, the party that made him finance minister and then negotiated around him, loses the government it won in 2015 in the same count.

stops.name: Athens, the drive the Speaker would not take
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the EuroLeaks release of March 2020, the refused USB deposit and the count of thirteen sessions come from the dossier and could not be corroborated anywhere reachable, the DiEM25 record not mentioning EuroLeaks at all; the day is an ordering device

The same year he publishes the novel Another Now, dispatches from an alternative present. DiEM25 then puts the audio and the transcripts of thirteen sessions online under the name EuroLeaks, on the argument that a body which legislates for a continent and keeps no minutes should not also own the only record of what it said.

stops.name: Athens, the invasion and the fracture
stops.date_confidence: the invasion is attested to the day; his position and the Razem departure from DiEM25 and the Progressive International come from the dossier's synthesis of 2022 statements and were not independently re-fetched
stops.campa: Russia invades Ukraine. It is the first serious fracture in the coalition assembled at the Volksbuhne six years earlier.

stops.name: Athens, Technofeudalism
stops.date_confidence: the 2023 publication is attested; no month recorded, and the stop is pinned at his university rather than at the London publisher
stops.campa: He publishes Technofeudalism: What Killed Capitalism, and the argument is that the thing Karl Marx anatomised is over. Profit taken through competitive markets has been displaced by cloud rent, the toll a handful of platforms levy on everything that crosses them, underwritten since 2008 by central banks pushing money into asset prices. Amazon, on this reading, is not a market but a fief, and its sellers are tenants. Here he says the object of the critique has changed shape. He has called himself an erratic Marxist, and then a libertarian Marxist.
stops.quote: I have long considered myself a libertarian Marxist.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to a Jacobin interview of 17 December 2020; seen only on Wikiquote, the original being unreachable for this file

stops.name: Exarchia, the table at Giantes
stops.date_confidence: the date and the fact of the attack are attested; the neighbourhood, the restaurant name and the multiple fracture are reconstruction, Wikipedia placing the assault only in central Athens and every outlet holding the detail having refused fetching
stops.campa: He is at dinner with DiEM25 colleagues at a restaurant in Exarchia, the quarter of Athens where the anarchist left holds the ground. A group comes to the table and accuses him of having signed the memoranda, the bailout agreements he resigned rather than sign. Then they hit him. He is punched and kicked outside the restaurant and his nose is broken in several places. Eight years have gone by since the memoranda, and on this street the accounting is not closed. Ten weeks later Greece goes to the polls.

stops.name: Evangelismos, the man who did not sign
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction on the same footing as the previous stop: the hospital and the injuries are dossier-sourced from ekathimerini reporting that could not be re-fetched
stops.campa: He is taken to Evangelismos, the big public hospital on the slope below Lycabettus, and treated for a fractured nose. The man beaten for signing the memoranda is the one member of the 2015 cabinet who resigned rather than sign one. From there he declines to turn the attack into a party matter and refuses to assign his attackers a political affiliation, though several are arrested. He accepts police protection afterwards at Danae Stratou's insistence rather than his own.

stops.name: Berlin, the ban and the court
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Palestine Congress was cut off on 12 April 2024 and his legal challenge is reported in May, but the dossier's sources were not re-fetched; the coordinate is the Berlin Administrative Court at Kirchstrasse 7 in Moabit, correcting a Wilmersdorf pin carried in the dossier
stops.campa: DiEM25 helps to organise a Palestine Congress in Berlin. German police cut the power and dissolve the gathering shortly after it opens, and Germany bars him from entering the country in connection with it. He sues. He has been out of the Greek parliament since May 2023, when MeRA25 fell under the threshold and lost all nine seats at once. In November 2025 the Berlin Administrative Court rules the dissolution unlawful and disproportionate, the police having found no evidence of any speech offence when they broke the congress up.

stops.name: Athens, five women and a century
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from a publisher listing (Bodley Head) dated 2 October 2025, which postdates the encyclopaedic snapshot used for the rest of this file and was not independently confirmed
stops.campa: He publishes Raise Your Soul: A Personal History of Resistance, and the subject this time is his own family: five women of his household and lineage, through whom he tells the last hundred years of Greek history. The occupation, the civil war, the colonels, the prisons and the memoranda arrive in the book as things that happened to a household rather than to a country. The man who spent a decade as the protagonist of 2015 writes himself in as the youngest person in the room. The publisher's listing does not name the five women.

stops.name: Athens, the summons over a night in Sydney
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the police summons is reported on 16 January 2026 and the referral to trial on 26 February 2026, but the dossier's earlier claim of a prosecutorial inquiry opened on 7 January could not be supported by anything reachable and is not used here
stops.campa: On a podcast he is asked about drugs and answers plainly: once, ecstasy, in Sydney, thirty-seven years ago. A prosecutor in Athens opens an inquiry into the remarks, and in the middle of January the police summon him over them. The charge concerns one sentence about one night in 1989, spoken into a microphone. In February he is sent to trial under Article 24 of the narcotics law for promotion of drug use, with a hearing set for the sixteenth of December. He is sixty-four.
stops.quote: I've taken ecstasy once, and it was an amazing experience... I remember dancing for 15-16 hours.
